QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_4

question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (open-ended Cat III) had a pre-side-pocket NAV of INR 100 per unit. An illiquid position representing 12% of gross assets is segregated into a side-pocket. What are the NAVs of the main and side-pocket units immediately post-segregation, assuming pari-passu allocation?

explanation.text: The Logic: When a side-pocket is created pari-passu, the pre-event NAV is split between the main (liquid) scheme and the side-pocket (illiquid) scheme in proportion to the value each segment represents in gross assets. The pre-event NAV is INR 100 per unit. The illiquid bucket is 12% of gross assets, so the side-pocket NAV/unit immediately after segregation is INR 12, while the main scheme NAV/unit is the remaining INR 88. The two together (12 + 88) sum back to the original INR 100, preserving total per-unit value. Each existing unit-holder receives one main unit and one side-pocket unit; new subscribers after segregation invest only in the main series. The Trap: Option A zeroes the side-pocket — wrong, because segregation transfers value across schemes rather than writing it off. Option C double-counts by valuing the side-pocket at the full pre-event NAV. Option D claims the main NAV is INR 112, which would imply a net increase in per-unit value with no underlying PnL — not possible from a pure segregation event. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (84, 310, 337) support NAV declaration and class/series-of-units allocation concepts but do not describe side-pocket creation, the pari-passu NAV split between main and side-pocket schemes, or post-segregation subscription/redemption mechanics. The framing above is general industry/fund-structuring practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
